# ScottSearch 0.1.3 — Verbose now means more context

This human-testing patch fixes a result-detail regression reported against
0.1.2. Switching from Default to Verbose could replace the compact preview
with fewer characters, making the two modes look the same.

## Fixed

- Verbose now extends the existing Default preview instead of replacing it
  with a potentially shorter excerpt.
- **Verbose result context** controls how many extra characters are added to
  both sides of the compact preview. The default remains 100, configurable
  from 20 through 1,000.
- Matches near the beginning, middle, and end of long notes all expand when
  more note text is available.
- Meaning-only results continue to preview from the beginning of the note.
- Switching detail modes still updates only presentation and does not repeat
  the search or regenerate a semantic query embedding.

## Privacy and compatibility

The fix changes local snippet construction only. It adds no network request and
does not change the existing local/offline privacy boundary. Optional Ollama
behavior is unchanged, and unreleased on-device experiments remain excluded
from the public bundle.

ScottSearch supports Obsidian 1.7.2 or later on macOS, Windows, Linux, iPhone,
iPad, and Android. This remains a pre-release for human testing rather than a
stable Community-directory submission.

## Install or update

BRAT users can update ScottSearch normally. For a manual installation,
download `scottsearch-0.1.3.zip` below, unzip it, place the enclosed
`scottsearch` folder inside `<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/`, restart Obsidian, and
enable ScottSearch under **Settings → Community plugins**.

Please report sanitized results through the
[friendly beta form](https://github.com/c4g-john/scottsearch-for-obsidian/issues/new?template=beta_test_report.yml).
Do not include private note text or credentials in public reports.

To roll back, reinstall 0.1.2 from its release page. Neither update nor rollback
deletes notes.
